Sample Name: General Medicine Followup - Hypertension and Diabetes
Description: Followup after negative sexually transmitted infection testing, with review of blood pressure, glucose control, and cardiovascular medications.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient was previously evaluated in urgent care for urethral burning or discharge. He states that these symptoms have resolved. HIV, syphilis, gonorrhea, and Chlamydia testing were reported as negative. He continues terazosin for urinary or prostate symptoms with nocturia. He drinks considerable sweetened lemonade, including in the evening. He has coronary artery disease treated with a coronary stent and has diabetes and hypertension. He stopped taking his blood pressure medication for approximately one month because home readings seemed low, and his home cuff recently stopped functioning. Clinic blood pressure today is 135/74. His last hemoglobin A1c in December was 6.4, improved from approximately 7. He takes metformin and would prefer to use fewer medicines. He reports adherence to aspirin and Plavix. His blood counts have declined somewhat compared with previous measurements, and he asks whether he may donate blood.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Coronary artery disease status post stent placement, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and prostate-related urinary symptoms.
MEDICATIONS: Metformin, terazosin, aspirin, Plavix, and previously prescribed antihypertensives including lisinopril; metoprolol was also discussed.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Blood pressure 135/74. No chest pain or shortness of breath was reported.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Hypertension in the setting of coronary artery disease and diabetes. Restart low-dose lisinopril, described at the conclusion of the visit as one-half tablet daily. Home blood pressure monitoring and a repeat office check in two weeks were arranged. The patient was asked to bring his monitor for comparison.
2. Type 2 diabetes, currently well controlled by A1c. A home glucometer was ordered. Record fasting or two-hour postprandial readings several times weekly. A trial off metformin could be considered if subsequent values remain satisfactory; discontinuation was not ordered at this visit.
3. Coronary artery disease. The importance of continuing aspirin and Plavix after stenting was emphasized.
4. Mild decline in blood count. Repeat CBC ordered before clearance for blood donation.
5. Resolved urethral symptoms. Reviewed negative sexually transmitted infection results and advised safe sexual practices. Continue terazosin and reduce late-evening fluid intake for nocturia.
Return in two weeks for blood pressure reassessment.
